questions.stem:
Eligibility for a Junior Research Fellowship (JRF): (i) Must have a postgraduate degree with at least 55% marks; (ii) Must have cleared the NET examination in the relevant subject; (iii) Age must not exceed 28 years as on 1 July of the application year; (iv) Relaxation of 5 years in age limit for SC/ST/OBC/PwD candidates.

Candidate: Nalini holds an M.Sc. in Chemistry with 61% marks and has cleared the NET in Chemistry. She belongs to the OBC category and is 31 years old as on 1 July of the application year.

What should be the decision?

options.option_text: Select: All criteria met — 61% ≥ 55%, NET cleared, and OBC relaxation makes her eligible at 31 (≤33)
Reject: Age exceeds 28 years without considering any relaxation provision
Refer to higher authority: marginal overqualification in marks
Reject: NET must be cleared in the same academic year as the application

questions.explanation: A is correct. Criterion (i): 61% ≥ 55% ✓. Criterion (ii): NET cleared in Chemistry ✓. Criterion (iii): Age limit is 28+5=33 for OBC candidates (criterion iv). Nalini is 31 ≤ 33 ✓. All criteria satisfied. Option B incorrectly ignores the OBC relaxation. Option D invents a condition not stated in the problem.

questions.stem:
Eligibility for a Bank Probationary Officer (PO) post: (i) Graduate degree in any discipline with at least 60% marks; (ii) Age between 21 and 30 years as on 1 January; (iii) Must be an Indian citizen; (iv) SC/ST candidates get a 5-year relaxation in age; (v) Candidates with banking experience of 2+ years get a 3% marks relaxation.

Candidate: Suresh has a B.Com. degree with 58% marks and has worked in a cooperative bank for 3 years. He is 29 years old, a general category Indian citizen.

What should be the decision?

options.option_text: Select: 3% marks relaxation brings effective minimum to 57%, and 58% ≥ 57%
Reject: 58% is below the required 60% and no relaxation removes this gap
Refer to higher authority: banking experience in cooperative banks may not qualify
Reject: 29 years exceeds the upper limit (without reading criterion ii correctly)

questions.explanation: A is correct. Criterion (i): Suresh has 58% but criterion (v) grants a 3% marks relaxation for candidates with 2+ years banking experience. Effective minimum = 60%−3% = 57%. 58% ≥ 57% ✓. Criterion (ii): Age 29 is between 21 and 30 ✓. Criterion (iii): Indian citizen ✓. The cooperative bank experience is not disqualified by any stated criterion. All criteria satisfied after applying relaxation (v). Option B ignores the marks relaxation in criterion (v). Option D misreads the age limit (30 is the upper, and Suresh is 29).

questions.stem:
Eligibility for a State Civil Services Preliminary Examination: (i) Must be a graduate in any discipline; (ii) Age must be between 21 and 35 years; (iii) Candidates already serving in state government with 5+ years of service get upper age limit relaxed to 40; (iv) A candidate can appear a maximum of 6 times.

Candidate: Deepak is a 37-year-old state government employee with 8 years of service. He has a B.A. degree and is appearing for the 5th time.

What should be the decision?

options.option_text: Select: Age relaxed to 40 for in-service candidates with 5+ years; 37 ≤ 40; attempt count 5 ≤ 6
Reject: Age 37 exceeds the 35-year limit applicable to all candidates
Reject: 5th attempt is the maximum permitted for government employees
Refer to higher authority: service period of 8 years in government may require verification

questions.explanation: A is correct. Criterion (i): B.A. degree ✓. Criterion (ii)+(iii): Deepak has 8 years of state government service ≥ 5 years, so upper age relaxed to 40. His age 37 ≤ 40 ✓. Criterion (iv): 5th attempt ≤ 6 ✓. All criteria satisfied. Option B incorrectly applies the general 35-year limit without considering the relaxation in criterion (iii). Option C invents a 5-attempt limit for government employees — the stated limit is 6 for all.

questions.stem:
Eligibility for a Government Scholarship for Higher Studies Abroad: (i) Must have secured at least 75% in the qualifying examination; (ii) Must be below 25 years of age; (iii) Must be an Indian citizen; (iv) Must not be employed or receiving any other government scholarship; (v) Sports persons with national-level representation get a 5% marks relaxation and 2-year age relaxation.

Candidate: Priya is 26 years old, has 72% in her degree, is an Indian citizen, and represented India in badminton at the national level. She is currently unemployed and not receiving any other scholarship.

What should be the decision?

options.option_text: Select: Sports relaxation → marks 72% ≥ 70%, age ≤ 27; Priya is 26 ≤ 27; all criteria met
Reject: 72% is below the required 75% even after the sports relaxation of 5%
Reject: Age 26 exceeds the 25-year limit applicable to all candidates
Refer to higher authority: sports representation must be verified before decision

questions.explanation: A is correct. Criterion (v): Priya has national-level sports representation → marks relaxation 5% (effective minimum: 75%−5%=70%) and age relaxation 2 years (effective limit: 25+2=27). Check: marks 72% ≥ 70% ✓; age 26 ≤ 27 ✓; Indian citizen ✓; not employed ✓; no other scholarship ✓. All criteria satisfied. Option B incorrectly computes 5% relaxation as making the threshold 80%, not 70%. Option C ignores the age relaxation for sports persons in criterion (v).

questions.stem:
Eligibility for a Loan from a Cooperative Bank: (i) Applicant must be a member of the cooperative for at least 2 years; (ii) Monthly income must be at least ₹20,000; (iii) Applicant must not have any outstanding dues with the cooperative; (iv) Loan amount must not exceed 80% of the applicant's monthly income × 36; (v) An existing borrower who has cleared 3 consecutive EMIs without default can apply for a top-up loan.

Candidate: Ramesh has been a cooperative member for 3 years. His monthly income is ₹18,000 and he has no outstanding dues. He is applying for a top-up loan and has paid 5 consecutive EMIs without default.

What should be the decision?

options.option_text: Select: Top-up loan eligible under criterion (v); criterion (ii) applies to new loans only
Reject: Monthly income ₹18,000 is below the ₹20,000 minimum required under criterion (ii)
Select: Criterion (v) overrides income criterion for top-up loans
Refer to higher authority: top-up loan policy may require board approval

questions.explanation: B is correct. Criterion (ii) specifies monthly income ≥ ₹20,000. Ramesh earns ₹18,000 < ₹20,000. Nothing in the stated criteria creates an exception to the income requirement for top-up loans. Criterion (v) addresses ELIGIBILITY to apply for a top-up loan based on repayment history — it does not waive the income requirement in criterion (ii). All general eligibility conditions still apply. Option A (and C) incorrectly assume criterion (v) creates a carve-out from criterion (ii). Option D invents a board-approval requirement not mentioned in the criteria.

questions.stem:
Eligibility for a Senior Citizen Pension Scheme: (i) Applicant must be 60 years of age or above; (ii) Annual family income must not exceed ₹1.5 lakh; (iii) Applicant must be a resident of the state for at least 10 years; (iv) Must not be receiving any other government pension or social security benefit; (v) Applicant with a disability certificate gets an age relaxation — eligible from 55 years.

Candidate: Kamla is 57 years old, has lived in the state for 15 years, and her annual family income is ₹90,000. She holds a government-issued disability certificate and is not receiving any other pension.

What should be the decision?

options.option_text: Reject: Age 57 is below the 60-year threshold required for senior citizens
Select: Disability certificate triggers age relaxation; 57 ≥ 55; all other criteria met
Refer to higher authority: disability certificate validity and type need verification
Reject: Family income of ₹90,000 disqualifies her under criterion (ii)

questions.explanation: B is correct. Criterion (v): disability certificate → age eligibility reduced to 55. Kamla is 57 ≥ 55 ✓. Criterion (i)+relaxation: satisfied. Criterion (ii): ₹90,000 < ₹1.5 lakh ✓. Criterion (iii): 15 years residency ≥ 10 ✓. Criterion (iv): not receiving other pension ✓. All criteria satisfied. Option A ignores the relaxation in criterion (v). Option D misreads the income criterion — ₹90,000 is BELOW the ₹1.5 lakh ceiling, so it qualifies (not disqualifies).

questions.stem:
Eligibility for a Teaching Post at a Government Degree College: (i) Must hold a Ph.D. in the relevant subject; (ii) Age must be below 40 years; (iii) Must have at least 3 years of teaching experience at a college or university; (iv) Candidates who have published at least 5 peer-reviewed papers may substitute teaching experience (only 1 year required in such cases); (v) SC/ST/OBC candidates get 5 years age relaxation.

Candidate: Dr. Anand holds a Ph.D. in Economics, is 38 years old, belongs to the OBC category, and has 1 year of teaching experience. He has published 7 peer-reviewed papers.

What should be the decision?

options.option_text: Select: Ph.D. ✓; age 38 < 45 (OBC relaxation) ✓; 7 papers ≥ 5 → only 1 year teaching required ✓
Reject: 1 year of teaching experience is below the required 3 years
Reject: OBC age relaxation not applicable when publications are used as a substitute
Refer to higher authority: verify whether publications are in approved journals

questions.explanation: A is correct. Criterion (i): Ph.D. in Economics ✓. Criterion (ii)+(v): OBC → age limit 40+5=45; Dr. Anand is 38 < 45 ✓. Criterion (iii)+(iv): 7 papers ≥ 5 → teaching requirement reduced to 1 year. He has exactly 1 year ✓. All criteria satisfied. Option B ignores criterion (iv) entirely. Option C invents a rule that OBC relaxation cannot coexist with the publication substitution — no such restriction is stated. Option D introduces a 'journal approval' requirement not in the criteria.

questions.stem:
Eligibility for an Apprenticeship under a Government Scheme: (i) Must have passed Class 10 from a recognised board; (ii) Age must be between 14 and 21 years; (iii) Must not be pursuing any full-time course at the time of registration; (iv) Must not have completed a previous apprenticeship under the same employer; (v) ITI certificate holders get priority, but non-ITI candidates can also apply.

Candidate: Mukesh passed Class 10 with 65% marks. He is 19 years old. He completed an ITI course last year and is not currently enrolled in any full-time course. He applied for apprenticeship under the same employer where he served as an apprentice 2 years ago.

What should be the decision?

options.option_text: Select: Class 10 ✓; age 19 ✓; not in full-time course ✓; ITI gives priority
Reject: Already completed apprenticeship with the same employer — disqualified by criterion (iv)
Refer to higher authority: ITI certification needs to be verified before decision
Select: ITI certification overrides criterion (iv) for priority candidates

questions.explanation: B is correct. Criterion (iv): Mukesh must not have completed a previous apprenticeship under the SAME employer. He did complete one 2 years ago with the same employer — this directly violates criterion (iv). Result: rejected. Note: the ITI certificate in criterion (v) gives priority status — it does not create an exemption from any other criterion. Option A ignores criterion (iv). Option D incorrectly treats priority status as an override of disqualifying conditions.

questions.stem:
Eligibility for a Housing Loan Subsidy under an Urban Housing Scheme: (i) Annual household income must be between ₹3 lakh and ₹18 lakh (Middle Income Group); (ii) The applicant or any family member must not own a pucca house anywhere in India; (iii) Must be an Indian citizen; (iv) Loan must be for purchase or construction of a first house; (v) The carpet area of the house must not exceed 160 sq.m.

Candidate: Rajiv earns ₹12 lakh per year. He is an Indian citizen. Neither he nor his wife owns any property. He wants a loan to purchase a flat of 155 sq.m. However, his father bought a house in Rajiv's name 15 years ago, which Rajiv was unaware of.

What should be the decision?

options.option_text: Select: Income ✓; citizenship ✓; flat size 155 ≤ 160 ✓; Rajiv was unaware of the house
Reject: A house already exists in Rajiv's name — criterion (ii) violated regardless of awareness
Refer to higher authority: his lack of awareness may be grounds for a waiver
Select: Property inherited without intent does not count as 'owned' under criterion (ii)

questions.explanation: B is correct. Criterion (ii) states the applicant must not own a pucca house anywhere in India. A house is registered in Rajiv's name — whether he was aware or not, legally he is the owner. The criterion makes no exception for involuntary or unknowing ownership. This is a common trap: the feeling of injustice ('he didn't know') draws candidates to options A or C, but the criterion is objective — ownership in name disqualifies. Option C (refer for waiver) invents a discretionary procedure not mentioned. Option D invents an 'intent' exception not stated.

questions.stem:
Eligibility for a District Level Sports Award: (i) Must be an Indian citizen; (ii) Must have represented the district in an inter-district or state-level competition in the past 2 years; (iii) Must be below 25 years of age; (iv) Must have won a medal or certificate of merit in at least one competition; (v) Professional athletes with any international contract are ineligible.

Candidate: Meena is 23 years old, an Indian citizen, and represented her district in the state swimming championship 18 months ago, finishing fourth. She received a certificate of participation but not a merit certificate. She has no international contract.

What should be the decision?

options.option_text: Select: Age ✓; citizenship ✓; represented district within 2 years ✓; no contract ✓
Reject: A certificate of participation is not a certificate of merit — criterion (iv) not satisfied
Refer to higher authority: fourth-place finish should be reviewed for merit status
Select: Representing the district itself satisfies criterion (iv) as merit is implied

questions.explanation: B is correct. Criterion (iv) requires a medal OR a certificate of merit. Meena received only a 'certificate of participation' — which is explicitly NOT a certificate of merit. A fourth-place finish does not earn a medal. All other criteria are met, but criterion (iv) fails. Option A ignores criterion (iv). Option C invents a review mechanism. Option D conflates 'participation' with 'merit' — the two are different in competitive sports contexts.
